summary: Lineup is already optimal — no changes. One free waiver claim worth making: Mark Andrews is unrostered and outprojects Pitts. Tuten is a committee back, not a lead back.

items.headline: Mark Andrews — claim, drop Stafford
items.body: Unrostered in this league. Likely and Kolar both left Baltimore; Andrews is the unchallenged TE1 on a Lamar Jackson offense and faces Indy, which allowed the 4th-most yards per target to TEs last year. ESPN projects 10.1 vs 7.6 for Pitts. Camp reports on his hands were poor, so this is a projection-and-role bet, not a lock. Priority resets weekly, so the claim costs nothing.

items.headline: Stafford is the drop
items.body: He is a QB2 behind Josh Allen in a 10-team 1-QB league, which is the lowest-value bench slot you own. He posted 4.1 on Thursday: 155 yards, one pick, no TDs in a 27-7 loss. 93% rostered, but rostered elsewhere as a starter, not as a backup. Allen's week 7 bye is streamable for free.

items.headline: Tuten is a co-starter, not a lead back
items.body: Jacksonville lists Tuten and Chris Rodriguez as co-starters and the beat expects a near-even split; the pre-season read that only an injured Rodriguez sat behind him is wrong. LeQuint Allen (hip) is trending toward sitting, which pushes pass-down work to Tuten. Still starts at RB2 — there is nothing better — but treat 10.9 as the ceiling case.

items.headline: Warren stays benched
items.body: Listed RB1 over Rico Dowdle, but McCarthy brought Dowdle in and the expectation is Dowdle gets early-down work with roughly a 3:2 touch edge in week 1. Warren was also limited Wednesday with a hip. His edge is receiving, which is worth half here.

items.headline: McLaurin holds the flex over Warren
items.body: Off the final injury report entirely, full practices Thursday and Friday, and Washington has cleared its full squad for Philadelphia. He is the unquestioned alpha with the OC targeting roughly 10 looks a game.

items.headline: Jaguars D/ST
items.body: Consensus number-one defense of the week. Cleveland starts Deshaun Watson behind the league's worst-graded offensive line, carries the lowest implied team total on the slate, and Jacksonville is a 7.5-point home favorite.

items.headline: De'Von Achane
items.body: Confirmed focal point of the Miami offense with no committee. Malik Willis' designed-run usage is the only real drag, and Miami is only a 3-point underdog.

items.headline: Allgeier may actually start for Arizona
items.body: Jeremiyah Love is questionable with the ankle and listed second on the depth chart; Allgeier is expected to open as the early-down back. ESPN's 6.9 projection has not caught up. Hold him over the other bench bodies.
